title: 2011 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: In \(1991\) the population of a town was a perfect square. Ten years later, after an increase of \(150\) people, the population was \(9\) more than a perfect square. Now, in \(2011,\) with an increase of another \(150\) people, the population is once again a perfect square. Which of the following is closest to the percent growth of the town’s population during this twenty-year period?

solutions.text:
Let the population in \(1991\) be \(p^2.\) Then let the population in \(2001\) be \(q^2 + 9.\)

Using these values, we have \[ p^2 + 150 = q^2 + 9 \] \[ q^2 - p^2 = 141. \]

Factoring, we get \[ (q - p)(q + p) = 141. \]

As \(p\) and \(q\) are integers, we have that the only possible values for \(q - p\) and \(q + p\) are \((1, 141)\) and \((3, 47).\)

Trying the first pair, we have \[q-p=1\] and \[q+p=141,\] which adding together and dividing gives us \(q = 71\) and \(p = 70.\)

We have that \(p^2 + 300\) is not a square number, which means that this pair is the wrong one.

Trying the other pair and using the same strategy gives us \(q = 25\) and \(p = 22.\)

Now, \(p^2 + 300 = 784,\) which is a perfect square. The percent increase in population is then \[ \dfrac{300}{22^2} \cdot 100 \% \approx 62 \%. \]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Use \((q-p)(q+p)=141\) and test the factor pairs
